blocks.title: Narrator and point of view
blocks.md: The **narrator** tells the story. **First person** (‘I’) gives a personal, limited view. **Third person limited** follows one character’s thoughts. **Omniscient** narration knows everything about all characters. The point of view controls what we know and how far we trust it.

blocks.title: Character, setting, language
blocks.md: **Characterisation** can be **direct** (the narrator tells us) or **indirect** (through actions, speech, thoughts, other characters’ reactions). **Setting** includes place, time and atmosphere. Look at **diction** (word choice), **imagery**, **sentence length** and **tone**, and always ask: what effect does this have on the reader?

blocks.caption: The four steps of a commentary.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: point, quotation, technique and effect.

blocks.title: A commentary in four steps
blocks.md: 1. State what is happening and who is speaking. 2. Pick a detail and quote a few words. 3. Name the technique (for example personification). 4. Explain the **effect**: what it shows about character, mood or theme. This is the **point, quotation, technique, effect** method.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Retelling the story instead of analysing the writing.
- Naming a technique without explaining its effect.
- Quoting long chunks: use short, precise quotations.
- Confusing the author with the narrator.

blocks.title: Example 1 — Point of view
blocks.statement: Original passage: ‘Mama Enow set out her tomatoes in the grey light, one red pyramid at a time. Across the lane the cloth seller’s radio was already arguing with itself. When her son’s footsteps came she did not look up; she knew them by their hesitation. A boy with something to confess walks as if the road were cold water.’ Identify the point of view.
steps: The narrator uses ‘she’ and ‘her’: third person.
We learn what Mama Enow knows (‘she knew them by their hesitation’).
So it is third-person limited, close to Mama Enow’s perception.
blocks.answer: Third-person limited, close to Mama Enow.

blocks.title: Example 2 — Effect of language
blocks.statement: Use the same passage: comment on ‘the cloth seller’s radio was already arguing with itself’.
steps: Technique: personification; the radio is given a human action.
It suggests overlapping stations and noise, so the market is busy and a little chaotic.
‘Already’ shows the day has only just begun, and contrasts with Mama’s calm.
blocks.answer: Personification creates noisy market atmosphere and contrasts with her calm.

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Original sentence: ‘The old mango tree leaned over the compound as if it wanted to hear the family’s secrets.’ Name the technique and explain its effect.
exercises.model: Personification: the tree is given the human wish to listen. The effect is to make the compound feel intimate and watchful, suggesting that secrets are present and creating a slightly mysterious atmosphere.
exercises.rubric: Technique (1); effect on atmosphere (2); use of quotation (1).
exercises.explanation: Personification: the tree is given the human wish to listen. The effect is to make the compound feel intimate and watchful, suggesting that secrets are present and creating a slightly mysterious atmosphere.

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Original passage: ‘Mr Tabot straightened his tie in the window of the closed bank, though no one was awake to see. His shoes were polished, his cuffs frayed.’ Write a short paragraph on what the details suggest about his character.
exercises.model: The straightened tie and polished shoes suggest pride and a wish to look respectable even when unobserved. The frayed cuffs contrast with this, suggesting that he is not wealthy and perhaps struggling. Together these indirect details show a dignified man hiding hardship.
exercises.rubric: Quoted detail (1); effect on character (2); contrast noted (1).
exercises.explanation: The straightened tie and polished shoes suggest pride and a wish to look respectable even when unobserved. The frayed cuffs contrast with this, suggesting that he is not wealthy and perhaps struggling. Together these indirect details show a dignified man hiding hardship.
